[ASSISTANT_SAID] The main character in "Catcher in the Rye," Holden Caulfield, is on a search for identity throughout the book.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Holden has been kicked out of school and is wandering the streets of New York City, trying to find his place in the world.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Holden struggles with connecting with other people and often feels alienated and disconnected from the world around him.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Holden criticizes people he sees as "phony" and longs for genuine connections with others.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Holden is searching for something meaningful to believe in, as he is disillusioned with his former beliefs and values.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Holden's rejection of societal norms and expectations reflects his skepticism of the adult world and refusal to conform.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Holden seeks authenticity and sincerity in others and in himself but is conflicted about his own authenticity.
